notes:
HOW FACTS WERE CHECKED. Every headcount in this file was read on the page it cites (fetched and searched for the figure). The web-search allowance ran out part-way through, so many plants have no headcount: they are null, not estimated. Existence and addresses of plants without a company page among their sources come from the EPA Toxics Release Inventory facility list for Texas (the URL in their sources), where each is listed as not closed, together with the researcher's general knowledge of the industry; they were not each re-confirmed on a 2026 company page. Product lines and opening years without a cited page are general knowledge and worth a second look. COORDINATES. Exact house-number matches from the geocoder were used where it gave one. Where it matched only the street, the EPA list's coordinate was used when it agreed with the street and with the known layout: Dow Freeport, Dow Deer Park, Dow Texas City, LyondellBasell La Porte and Houston Refinery, BASF Port Arthur, INEOS Chocolate Bayou, Battleground, Texas City and Green Lake, OxyChem La Porte, Pasadena and Battleground, Westlake Epoxy, Ketjen Bayport and Pasadena, Ascend, Indorama, Arkema Clear Lake, Chemours Corpus Christi, Shintech, Valero Port Arthur and Three Rivers, Phillips 66 Sweeny, CITGO, both Flint Hills plants, TotalEnergies La Porte, Delek Big Spring, Air Liquide Bayport, Linde Texas City. EPA coordinates are rounded to seconds and some are inside the fence rather than at the gate. Street-level points (on the right road beside the plant, not a house number) were accepted for: Gulf Coast Growth Ventures (FM 2986), LyondellBasell Corpus Christi (McKinzie Rd), Westlake Longview (Estes Dr), Celanese Bishop (County Road 4), and the Phillips 66 and Chevron Phillips plants at Borger (both on Spur 119, given the same point). These are the first to re-check. Wikipedia coordinates were used for ExxonMobil Baytown, Pemex Deer Park and Valero McKee. Olin Freeport is inside the Dow complex and shares its point; INVISTA Victoria and LyondellBasell Victoria are neighbours on one site and geocode to almost the same point. HEADCOUNT CAVEATS. ExxonMobil Baytown (7,000) is Harris County's figure and almost certainly counts contractors. Figures taken from undated pages (Valero and Phillips 66 refinery pages, the Victoria and Brazosport lists, the BASF Texas total) carry 2026, the year they were read. LyondellBasell's fact sheets say "Total Employees" without saying whether contractors are in. The Chevron Phillips Sweeny and OxyChem Texas figures include contractors by the companies' own wording. FIGURES SEEN ONLY IN SEARCH SUMMARIES AND LEFT OUT (the company sites refused automated requests or the page could not be opened): ExxonMobil's 2026 Baytown fact sheet, about 1,900 employees and 4,800 contract personnel (corporate.exxonmobil.com); Dow's Texas flyer, 2022: Freeport 3,666 employees and 2,450 contractors, Seadrift 726 and 563, Texas 7,198 employees (corporate.dow.com/content/dam/corp/documents/location/dow-in-texas-flyer.pdf); Dow Deer Park "nearly 700" and Texas City 330 (corporate.dow.com location pages); Eastman Longview "over 1,500"; Marathon Galveston Bay 1,550 and Motiva Port Arthur 1,450 (Wikipedia infoboxes, undated); TotalEnergies Port Arthur about 650; CITGO Corpus Christi "more than 1,000 jobs locally" (a 2017 company release that does not separate contractors). A reviewer with a browser can confirm these quickly. JUDGMENT CALLS. ExxonMobil's Baytown refinery, chemical plant and olefins plant are one plant; Beaumont refinery, chemical and lubricants are one plant with the polyethylene plant on Highway 90 kept apart. Valero's two Corpus Christi refineries are one plant because the company reports them together; Flint Hills' two are kept apart. BASF TotalEnergies Petrochemicals is listed as a BASF plant (60% owner and operator). Pemex Deer Park is its own company with parent Pemex; Shell keeps the chemical plant on the same site. OxyChem's parent is given as Berkshire Hathaway on the strength of reports that the purchase closed on 2 January 2026 (not opened on a primary page). Covestro's parent is given as XRG (ADNOC) from the Baytown foundation's report. Goodyear agreed in 2025 to sell its chemical business, which includes the Beaumont and Houston plants; whether the sale closed and what the business is now called could not be checked, so the plants are still listed under Goodyear. CITGO's ownership was the subject of a court-ordered sale and its parent is left null. LyondellBasell's Houston Refinery is listed as closed (refining ended in 2025). LEFT OUT FOR LACK OF A CHECKED SOURCE OR ADDRESS: AbbVie (Allergan) Waco, Fujifilm Biotechnologies College Station, Lonza Houston and Mary Kay Lewisville (pharmaceuticals and cosmetics); Nan Ya Plastics Wharton, Berry Global, Advanced Drainage Systems, Diamond Plastics, Charlotte Pipe, Pactiv (plastics); Orion and Cabot (carbon black), TPC Group, Kuraray, Evonik, Nouryon, Solvay/Syensqo, Sasol, Lion Elastomers, Arlanxeo, MEGlobal, Nutrien Borger (chemicals); GAF and Owens Corning (asphalt roofing); Ergon (asphalt terminals, not plants); Continental (no rubber plant in Texas was confirmed); Bridgestone's Firestone Polymers plant at Orange; Goodyear's Bayport plant; Dow's smaller La Porte, Bayport and Beaumont units.

V2, OSHA PASS (18 November 2026). Headcounts that were missing have been filled from OSHA's Form 300A establishment data (https://www.osha.gov/Establishment-Specific-Injury-and-Illness-Data): the files for reporting year 2025 and, where an establishment has no 2025 row, 2024, read from the copies on disk. The figure is the establishment's own 'annual average number of employees': that employer's people at that address, offices on the site included, contractors not included. A row was taken only when it had the same street address in the same city, or the same ZIP code and a name that is plainly this plant; each employeesNote names the row. Contractors' filings from the same address (maintenance, scaffolding, catering, security) were never used. Nothing else was changed except as listed here. Web search was not available, so nothing in this pass was checked against a company page. SCOPE RULE (construction is not manufacturing: no ready-mix, concrete block, pipe or precast, NAICS 3273, and no asphalt paving mixtures, 324121): no plant in this file is one of those, so none was removed. COUNTS: 58 plants filled (52 from the 2025 file, 6 from 2024); 6 still without a figure; 9 existing figures annotated with a differing OSHA figure; 87 of 93 plants now carry a headcount. OPERATING STATUS: for 33 plants that the earlier research could not confirm as operating, the note now says that a filing from the address is good evidence it was operating that year (OSHA's page is added to the plant's sources). NOT FILLED, AND WHY. Dow Deer Park: OSHA shows 2,145 for 2025 and 1,313 for 2024 at 1900 Tidal Rd, against the company's 'nearly 700' quoted in this file's earlier notes; the filing looks as if it carries other Houston-area Dow staff, so it was not used. Dow Texas City carries 722 (2025) with a caution in its note (394 in 2024; hours that fit about 500 people). Flint Hills East Refinery: the 2024 filing (88 people, 697,000 hours) does not hold together and there is none for 2025; the West Refinery carries its 2024 figure (964), which may cover staff shared by both plants. LyondellBasell Houston Refinery is marked closed and was left without a figure (its 2025 filing, 374, is the average while it was winding down). No filing found: Arkema Crosby, Linde Deer Park, JM Eagle Wharton. GOODYEAR: both chemical plants filed for 2025 as 'G-3 Chickadee Purchaser, LLC', so the sale the earlier researcher could not confirm appears to have closed; the plants are still listed under Goodyear because the new operating name was not confirmed, and a reviewer should rename the company. LINDE Texas City (24) is one small unit at the listed address; Linde files its other Texas City units separately. SHINTECH Freeport (193) is Shintech's own staff; a maintenance contractor files 522 at the neighbouring address. CORRECTION: the plant 'Alcon Fort Worth' was removed from this file because texas-food-consumer.json carries the same campus under the same company ('Alcon Fort Worth Campus'); one copy is kept there. COMPARISONS: where a plant already had a figure from another source and OSHA differs by more than a fifth, the OSHA figure was added to the note and the figure left alone: ExxonMobil Baytown (7,000 against 2,481 for the refinery, chemical plant and olefins plant together) and Beaumont (2,100 against 1,639), Dow Seadrift (587 against 851), Chevron Phillips Sweeny (1,000 including contractors against 672) and LyondellBasell's Channelview, La Porte, Bayport, Corpus Christi and Victoria fact-sheet totals, which run a quarter to a third above the OSHA figures and probably count contractors. OSHA rows exist for three of this file's unplaced sites: Dow Sabine River Operations (863; now placed in texas-osha-additions.json), LyondellBasell Matagorda (161) and Marathon El Paso (468; filed from 1601 Trowbridge Dr, not the 6500 this file gives, so still unplaced).
